title: PM Zaidi Formally Assumes Office from Al-Sudani in Baghdad Handover Ceremony
detail: Ali al-Zaidi officially assumed the duties of Prime Minister and Supreme Commander of the Iraqi Armed Forces on May 16 in a formal handover ceremony with outgoing PM Mohammed Shia al-Sudani at the Council of Ministers building in Baghdad's Green Zone. Al-Sudani praised the democratic process and expressed confidence in Zaidi's leadership. In his first address as prime minister, Zaidi pledged economic reform, an anti-corruption drive, ensuring public service delivery, and achieving 'real national partnership' between Shia, Sunni, and Kurdish communities. He announced plans to convene a national economic conference within 60 days to present a comprehensive reform roadmap aligned with his 14-pillar governance program. Zaidi also confirmed that US-Iraq defense cooperation would continue, including the September 2026 troop transition framework, and pledged to address the PMF integration into state structures 'according to the constitution.' Iraqi and international observers noted the ceremony as a historically significant moment: the peaceful transfer of power between two elected prime ministers, a stability benchmark that had eluded Iraq for much of its modern history.

media.caption: PM Zaidi formally assumes office from al-Sudani in Baghdad handover ceremony — pledges economic reform and national partnership

title: US Charges Iraqi Kata'ib Hezbollah Commander with New York Synagogue Bomb Plot
detail: US federal prosecutors in New York, in coordination with Turkish authorities, announced on May 16 the arrest and charging of Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, 32, an Iraqi commander in the Iran-aligned Kata'ib Hezbollah (KH) militia. Al-Saadi was charged with organizing at least 18 attacks and planned attacks across the United States, Canada, and Europe, including a bomb plot targeting a synagogue in New York City and Jewish community centers in Los Angeles and Scottsdale, Arizona. Prosecutors alleged al-Saadi paid approximately $3,000 in cryptocurrency to an undercover US law enforcement officer posing as a Mexican cartel member. Al-Saadi allegedly operated a front organization called Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiyah. The charges represented the most significant KH-linked terrorism prosecution on US soil and added significant pressure on Baghdad, as the new Zaidi government was called upon by Washington to condemn the plot. KH's political wing in Iraq — Sadiqoun party — denied al-Saadi had any connection to KH's leadership or operations and called the charges 'fabricated.'

media.caption: US charges Iraqi Kata'ib Hezbollah commander with New York synagogue bomb plot — 18 planned attacks across US, Canada, Europe
